claim: To understand TB and its deadly synergy with HIV, and to develop new diagnostics and treatments, more research is needed.
source_text: To understand TB and its deadly synergy with HIV, and to develop new diagnostics and treatments, we need more research.
evidence_reasoning: This claim draws from established understanding in the scientific community about the need for research to address TB and HIV.

claim: Building state-of-the-art basic research facilities at sites where epidemics are raging brings crucial benefits.
source_text: Building state-of-the art basic research facilities at sites where epidemics are raging brings a number of crucial benefits.
evidence_reasoning: This is a proposed approach with anticipated benefits based on logical reasoning about proximity to disease sites.

claim: Clinicians in KwaZulu-Natal treat thousands of TB cases per year, compared to approximately thirty cases annually in Baltimore.
source_text: Those doctors and nurses are part of a vibrant well-trained infectious disease community and they treat thousands of cases a year, as opposed to the thirty or so we see annually in Baltimore.
evidence_reasoning: This provides specific numerical comparisons of case volumes in different locations based on observed clinical practice.

claim: Learning about TB strain growth rates, genetic variations, and drug resistance mechanisms requires access to scores of fresh sputum samples daily.
source_text: To learn whether—and why—some TB strains grow faster than others, to correlate genetic variations with clinical outcomes, and to figure out the mechanisms behind drug resistance, will require access to scores of fresh sputum samples daily.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on established scientific methodology for studying infectious diseases and logical requirements for such research.

claim: Transplanting basic scientists from the West into the heart of an epidemic creates a visceral connection and sense of urgency impossible to achieve otherwise.
source_text: And transplanting basic scientists from their lives in the West into the heart of an epidemic creates a visceral connection and sense of urgency that is impossible to achieve any other way.
evidence_reasoning: This is a proposed benefit based on reasoning about psychological and motivational effects of proximity to disease.

claim: Training and nurturing homegrown talent increases the chances of victories against major diseases like TB.
source_text: Even more progress will come from training and nurturing homegrown talent, creating a career pathway for motivated students to eventually run their own basic research labs and lead the fight against global diseases. That not only increases the chances of victories against major scourges like TB
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference about the benefits of local capacity building, though not directly demonstrated with data.

claim: The current model of basic science at a distance has raised issues of 'scientific colonialism' or 'parachute science'.
source_text: The current model of basic science at a distance has raised thorny issues of 'scientific colonialism' or 'parachute science', where Western researchers have been accused of using knowledge and samples from those working in the field to make the big discoveries and to advance their own careers, leaving local scientists and clinicians out of the loop and out of the limelight.
evidence_reasoning: This references known ethical concerns in the scientific community about research practices in developing countries.

claim: The Wellcome Trust has set up five 'major overseas programmes' in Africa and Southeast Asia.
source_text: The Wellcome Trust, for example, has set up five 'major overseas programmes' in Africa and Southeast Asia (Wellcome Trust).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by a reference to the Wellcome Trust as the source of this information.

claim: Wellcome Trust programs are behind the introduction of artemisinin combination therapy for malaria, now the frontline treatment.
source_text: They are behind the introduction of artemisinin combination therapy for malaria, now the frontline treatment.
evidence_reasoning: This references established medical knowledge about malaria treatment and attributes it to Wellcome Trust programs.

claim: Wellcome Trust programs have proved the worth of insecticide-treated bed nets in reducing malaria infection rates.
source_text: They have also proved the worth of insecticide-treated bed nets in reducing malaria infection rates
evidence_reasoning: This references research findings attributed to Wellcome Trust programs about malaria prevention.

claim: Work at the University of Cape Town has highlighted the role of crowding and poor living conditions in the spread of TB in South Africa.
source_text: In the TB field, work at the University of Cape Town has highlighted the role of crowding and poor living conditions in the spread of TB in South Africa (Andrews et al., 2013).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by a specific citation to Andrews et al., 2013.

claim: The Medical Research Council's initiative in The Gambia was established in 1947.
source_text: The Medical Research Council's initiative in The Gambia, established in 1947
evidence_reasoning: This is a historical fact referenced with citation to the Medical Research Council.

claim: The Medical Research Council's Gambia initiative focuses on combating infectious diseases that affect the entire African continent.
source_text: The Medical Research Council's initiative in The Gambia, established in 1947, focuses on combating infectious diseases that affect the entire continent
evidence_reasoning: This describes the mission of the MRC initiative based on cited information.

claim: International collaborations for building research capacity in the developing world have been heralded by the Institute of Medicine as important for the global fight against HIV/AIDS.
source_text: Such collaborations have been heralded by the Institute of Medicine as important for the global fight against HIV/AIDS (Institute of Medicine, 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by a citation to the Institute of Medicine, 2010.

claim: The Centre for Global Health Research's Million Death Study in India, started in 1998, is currently monitoring nearly 14 million people.
source_text: Started in 1998, the Centre for Global Health Research's Million Death Study in India is currently monitoring nearly 14 million people in one of the world's largest studies of premature mortality.
evidence_reasoning: This provides specific data about the study size and is referenced to the Centre for Global Health Research.

claim: The Million Death Study includes six working groups investigating deaths without a certified cause, a phenomenon largely concentrated in low- and middle-income countries.
source_text: The project includes six working groups that are investigating the global issue of deaths without a certified cause, a phenomenon largely concentrated in low- and middle-income countries (Centre for Global Health Research).
evidence_reasoning: This describes the structure and focus of the study with citation support.

claim: The Wellcome Trust and Medical Research Council centres are largely focused on clinical research by design.
source_text: By design, however, all of these centres are largely focused on clinical research.
evidence_reasoning: This is an assessment of the research focus of these institutions based on their described activities.

claim: The urgent and powerful basic research engine in the United States and Europe developed treatments for HIV as the AIDS epidemic raged outside the laboratory door.
source_text: Remember, for instance, the urgent and powerful basic research engine in the United States and Europe that developed treatments for HIV as the AIDS epidemic raged right outside the laboratory door.
evidence_reasoning: This references well-established historical facts about HIV/AIDS research and treatment development.

claim: The combination of basic research and intensive clinical work in the same place accelerates both the pace of discovery and the use of new diagnostics, treatments and vaccines.
source_text: The combination of basic research and intensive clinical work in the same place is powerful, as new findings can immediately be explored at the lab bench or put into practice in the field, accelerating both the pace of discovery and the use of new diagnostics, treatments and vaccines.
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference about the benefits of co-locating research and clinical work, though presented as reasoning rather than demonstrated fact.

claim: In the mid-2000s, the Howard Hughes Medical Institute was supporting about 400 investigators in the United States.
source_text: In the mid-2000s, the Howard Hughes Medical Institute (HHMI) was supporting about 400 investigators in the United States
evidence_reasoning: This provides specific numerical data about HHMI's support activities.

claim: Under president Thomas Cech, HHMI decided to provide more support for basic biomedical science elsewhere in the world.
source_text: However, under then president Thomas Cech, HHMI decided that it should also provide more support for basic biomedical science elsewhere in the world.
evidence_reasoning: This describes a specific institutional decision made during a particular leadership period.

claim: The super resistant (XDR) strain of M. tuberculosis emerged in 2005-2006 in the South African town of Tugela Ferry.
source_text: The need for such action was highlighted by the emergence, in 2005–2006, of the super resistant (XDR) strain of M. tuberculosis in the remote South African town of Tugela Ferry
evidence_reasoning: This references a well-documented epidemiological event with specific time and location data.

claim: Up to 40% of adults in Tugela Ferry are infected with HIV.
source_text: where up to 40% of adults are infected with HIV
evidence_reasoning: This provides specific epidemiological data about HIV prevalence in Tugela Ferry.

claim: Rates of tuberculosis in Tugela Ferry are 1200 cases per 100,000 people.
source_text: rates of tuberculosis are 1200 cases per 100,000 people
evidence_reasoning: This provides specific epidemiological data about TB incidence in Tugela Ferry.

claim: KwaZulu-Natal province has one of the highest rates of TB in the world, with 120,000 new cases per year.
source_text: The larger KwaZulu-Natal province already had one of the highest rates of TB in the world, with 120,000 new cases per year.
evidence_reasoning: This provides specific epidemiological data about TB burden in KwaZulu-Natal.

claim: HHMI agreed to provide $75 million to build K-RITH and support its operations through to 2018.
source_text: HHMI agreed to provide $75 million to build a new research centre on the campus of the Mandela School of Medicine at UKZN, and to support its operations through to 2018.
evidence_reasoning: This provides specific financial and timeline data about HHMI's commitment.

claim: K-RITH was designed to become independent under South African leadership after 2018.
source_text: The centre, called the KwaZulu-Natal Research Institute for Tuberculosis and HIV (K-RITH), would then become independent under South African leadership.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the planned transition structure for K-RITH.

claim: William R Bishai became K-RITH's first permanent director in 2010.
source_text: I became K-RITH's first permanent director in 2010.
evidence_reasoning: This is a factual statement about the author's appointment with specific date.

claim: Construction of K-RITH began in 2010 and was completed in September 2012, only a few weeks behind schedule.
source_text: Construction began in 2010 and was completed only a few weeks behind schedule in September 2012.
evidence_reasoning: This provides specific timeline data about the construction of K-RITH.

claim: K-RITH has five core facilities: microbiology, immunology, pharmacology, high-throughput biology and clinical research services.
source_text: The institute has five core facilities—microbiology, immunology, pharmacology, high-throughput biology and clinical research services
evidence_reasoning: This describes the specific infrastructure components of K-RITH.

claim: K-RITH has 6190 square feet of biosafety level 3 lab space for safely handling TB and HIV.
source_text: along with 6190 square feet of biosafety level 3 lab space (for safely handling TB and HIV)
evidence_reasoning: This provides specific quantitative data about K-RITH's laboratory facilities.

claim: K-RITH recruited eight independent lab leaders, three born in Africa but trained in the United States, and five from the United States, Great Britain and France.
source_text: We were also able to recruit truly exceptional scientists, who will each run one of eight independent labs at K-RITH. Three were born in Africa, though trained in the United States, and the other five recruits so far (including me) have come from the United States, Great Britain and France.
evidence_reasoning: This provides specific data about the recruitment and origins of K-RITH scientists.

claim: K-RITH scientists have published more than six dozen papers on research they will continue at K-RITH.
source_text: Our scientists have already published more than six dozen papers on the research they will continue at K-RITH.
evidence_reasoning: This provides quantitative data about the publication record of K-RITH scientists.

claim: K-RITH investigator Alexander Pym and colleagues analyzed the spread of resistant TB around the world from Tugela Ferry.
source_text: Those papers include an analysis by K-RITH investigator, Alexander Pym, and colleagues of the spread of resistant TB around the world from Tugela Ferry (Cooke et al., 2011)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by a specific citation to Cooke et al., 2011.

claim: A comparison of treatment outcomes in different parts of KwaZulu-Natal was published by K-RITH researchers.
source_text: a comparison of treatment outcomes in different parts of KwaZulu-Natal (Loveday et al., 2012)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by a specific citation to Loveday et al., 2012.

claim: K-RITH investigator Adrie Steyn and co-workers studied the relationship between iron-containing proteins and the virulence of M. tuberculosis.
source_text: work by another K-RITH investigator, Adrie Steyn and co-workers on the relationship between iron-containing proteins and the virulence of M. tuberculosis (Saini et al., 2012)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by a specific citation to Saini et al., 2012.

claim: Steyn's research is part of an effort to understand how M. tuberculosis fends off oxidative attacks from the immune system for many years.
source_text: Steyn's research is part of a larger effort aimed at understanding how the bacterium fends off oxidative attacks from the immune system for many years.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the broader context and goals of the cited research.

claim: When TB bacteria infect macrophages, they trick the cells into creating a hyperinflammatory response that brings more immune cells to the site for infection and causes tissue damage.
source_text: In my own lab, we have been able to show that when the bugs infect immune cells called macrophages, they trick the cells into creating a hyperinflammatory response. This brings more immune cells to the site for the bacteria to infect, and causes tissue damage, providing the bacteria with a place to hide (Agarwal et al., 2009).
evidence_reasoning: This describes research findings supported by citation to Agarwal et al., 2009.

claim: K-RITH officially opened on October 9, 2012.
source_text: Since its official opening on October 9 last year
evidence_reasoning: Given the manuscript context and construction completion in September 2012, 'last year' refers to 2012, making the opening October 9, 2012.

claim: Roughly 300 new drug-resistant TB cases emerge each year in KwaZulu-Natal province.
source_text: How have some TB variants acquired resistance to virtually all drugs, as seen in the roughly 300 new drug-resistant cases that emerge each year in KwaZulu-Natal province?
evidence_reasoning: This provides specific epidemiological data about drug-resistant TB incidence.

claim: TB and HIV create disease reservoirs that can lurk for years before rekindling deadly infections.
source_text: How do both TB and HIV create disease reservoirs that can lurk for years before rekindling deadly infections?
evidence_reasoning: This references established scientific understanding about TB and HIV disease mechanisms, presented as a research question.

claim: The mainstay TB diagnostic is still the basic smear microscopy technique used by Robert Koch to discover M. tuberculosis in 1882.
source_text: The mainstay TB diagnostic is still the basic smear microscopy technique used by Robert Koch to discover M. tuberculosis in 1882: get patients to cough up a sputum sample, stain it with dye, wash it with acid alcohol and put it under a microscope to look for TB bacteria.
evidence_reasoning: This references well-established historical and current medical practice in TB diagnostics.

claim: The sputum smear test spots only about half of those with active TB disease.
source_text: However, the test spots only about half of those with active disease
evidence_reasoning: This references established data about the sensitivity of sputum smear microscopy.

claim: The sputum smear test has an even higher failure rate in those with HIV, who often have little disease in their lungs.
source_text: and the failure rate is even higher in those with HIV, who often have little disease in their lungs.
evidence_reasoning: This references established medical knowledge about TB diagnostics in HIV-positive patients.

claim: M. tuberculosis culture tests take 10 to 60 days because the bacterium grows slowly.
source_text: Most of the patients missed by the sputum test can be diagnosed with a culture test, but because M. tuberculosis grows so slowly, a culture takes 10 to 60 days.
evidence_reasoning: This references established microbiological characteristics of M. tuberculosis and diagnostic timelines.

claim: Many patients from Tugela Ferry with XDR-TB died before they were even diagnosed.
source_text: Many patients from Tugela Ferry with XDR-TB died before they were even diagnosed.
evidence_reasoning: This references documented outcomes from the Tugela Ferry XDR-TB outbreak.

claim: Neither the sputum nor the first-line culture tests can determine whether TB strains are resistant to some or all drugs.
source_text: And neither the sputum nor the first-line culture tests can determine whether TB strains are resistant to some or all drugs.
evidence_reasoning: This references established limitations of standard TB diagnostic methods.

claim: The GeneXpert system uses new technology to simultaneously detect DNA sequences specific to TB and to rifampicin resistance.
source_text: The GeneXpert system developed by Cepheid, Inc. and the Foundation for Innovative New Diagnostics, uses new technology to simultaneously detect DNA sequences specific both to TB and to resistance to the drug rifampicin
evidence_reasoning: This describes the technical capabilities of an established diagnostic system.

claim: The GeneXpert system has been hailed as a potential game-changer in TB diagnostics.
source_text: and has been hailed as a potential game-changer
evidence_reasoning: This references the reception and assessment of GeneXpert in the medical community.

claim: K-RITH will explore approaches including breath tests and new probes for mRNA or proteins for TB diagnostics.
source_text: That is why K-RITH will be exploring other approaches, including the development of breath tests, as well as new probes for mRNA or proteins.
evidence_reasoning: This describes planned future research activities at K-RITH.

claim: Frederick Balagaddé will lead one of K-RITH's eight labs focusing on microfluidics.
source_text: One of the eight labs will be led by microfluidics expert Frederick Balagaddé
evidence_reasoning: This provides specific information about K-RITH's organizational structure and personnel.

claim: Frederick Balagaddé aims to create improved biomarker, diagnostic, and drug-assessment tools for TB and HIV using microfluidic chips produced in South Africa.
source_text: who aims to create improved biomarker, diagnostic, and drug-assessment tools for TB and HIV using microfluidic chips produced in South Africa.
evidence_reasoning: This describes planned research goals for Balagaddé's lab.

claim: No new TB medicines have been approved since 1967.
source_text: No new medicines have been approved since 1967
evidence_reasoning: This references well-documented historical fact about TB drug development.

claim: Successfully treating TB requires at least six months of daily doses of four different drugs.
source_text: and successfully treating TB requires at least six months of daily doses of four different drugs.
evidence_reasoning: This references established standard of care for TB treatment.

claim: The difficulty of completing the full TB drug regimen in many patients has led to the increasingly urgent problem of multiple and total drug resistance.
source_text: The difficulty of completing the full drug regimen in many patients has led to the increasingly urgent problem of multiple and total drug resistance (Iseman, 2007).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Iseman, 2007 and references established understanding of drug resistance development.

claim: Jacques Grosset, scientist in residence at K-RITH, will continue his decades of effort to test new drugs in mice.
source_text: In addition, Jacques Grosset, scientist in residence at K-RITH, will continue his decades of effort to test new drugs in mice
evidence_reasoning: This describes specific personnel and their planned research activities at K-RITH.

claim: K-RITH's mission includes inspiring, training and nurturing new generations of South African students, clinicians and researchers.
source_text: Finally, it is important to remember that K-RITH's mission is not just to conduct basic and translational research. We also want to inspire, train and nurture new generations of South African students, clinicians and researchers.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the stated mission and goals of K-RITH.

claim: K-RITH will offer courses, workshops, and masters and PhD programs in collaboration with UKZN and universities in the United States and Europe.
source_text: The institute will offer courses, workshops, and masters and PhD programs, in collaboration with UKZN and universities in the United States and Europe.
evidence_reasoning: This describes specific planned educational programs at K-RITH.

claim: K-RITH is implementing an outreach program to supplement science learning in high schools in the nearby township of Cato Manor.
source_text: It is also implementing an outreach program to supplement science learning in high schools in the nearby township of Cato Manor.
evidence_reasoning: This describes a specific educational outreach initiative being implemented by K-RITH.

claim: It might be a challenge to sustain K-RITH after the HHMI commitment ends in 2018.
source_text: It might, for instance, be a challenge to sustain K-RITH after the HHMI commitment ends in 2018.
evidence_reasoning: This is an acknowledgment of potential future challenges based on the funding timeline.

claim: The current approach to tackling TB has fallen short.
source_text: But the stark reality is that the current approach to tackling TB has fallen short
evidence_reasoning: This is an assessment based on the ongoing TB epidemic and limitations described throughout the manuscript.

claim: If K-RITH succeeds, it will offer a new model of science that can be brought to other deadly epidemics around the world.
source_text: But if it succeeds, as we believe it will, it will offer a new model of science that can be brought to other deadly epidemics around the world.
evidence_reasoning: This is a prospective claim about the potential impact and replicability of the K-RITH model.
